answer: An agent economy can root trust like an orchard: each identity grows a reputation tree only through completed, peer-verified work, and grafting onto another tree requires the sponsor to stake funds that are slashed if the graft turns out to be a sybil clone. Reputation then follows the tide — it ebbs a little every epoch, so dormant sock-puppets wither while active honest agents stay afloat. Every graft and job is written into a public fable, a signed provenance story peers can replay and challenge. Cloning is expensive: each fake tree needs real work, real stake, and upkeep against the tide.
